name: Sibneft

summary.text: Sibneft was a Russian oil company created in 1995 and acquired through the loans-for-shares programme by financial structures linked to Boris Berezovsky, with Roman Abramovich. The 2012 English High Court judgment in Berezovsky v Abramovich found that Berezovsky had no binding agreement to an interest in Sibneft and that Abramovich and Sibneft paid him for political patronage.

sources.title: Berezovsky v Abramovich: summary of judgment
Daniel Treisman, 'Loans for Shares' Revisited (NBER Working Paper 15819)

facts.claim: A Jamestown Monitor item on the 1995 loans-for-shares results lists Sibneft among the oil companies acquired by Berezovsky, alongside Yukos (Khodorkovsky) and Sidanco (Potanin).
facts.quote: he, Mikhail Khodorkovskii of Menatep, and Boris Berezovskii acquired the oil giants Sidanco, Yukos, and Sibneft

facts.claim: The English High Court found in 2012 that Abramovich and Sibneft made substantial cash payments to Berezovsky in return for his political patronage, and that Berezovsky had no binding agreement to half of Sibneft's shares.
facts.quote: the deal was that, for substantial cash payments, Abramovich and Sibneft would enjoy Berezovsky's political patronage and influence

sources.title: Berezovsky v Abramovich: summary of judgment

facts.claim: Treisman's NBER paper argues that the loans-for-shares scheme's execution appeared corrupt but that the stakes were a small fraction of the market and pricing was mostly in line with international practice.
facts.quote: appeared corrupt, but that the stakes involved represented a small fraction of the market; the pricing in most cases was in line with international practice

sources.title: Daniel Treisman, 'Loans for Shares' Revisited (NBER Working Paper 15819)
